commits.author: sebpet182
commits.message:
Updated and fixed for 2026 Spotify API reworks
See here: https://developer.spotify.com/blog/2026-02-06-update-on-developer-access-and-platform-security

- "Appears-on" is completely dead due to the removal of the AlbumGroup field, and all instances/attempts/references to it have been from the source. This is probably the biggest change, but I really can't be bothered to rework everything from scratch for this. RIP
- At least the aforementioned removal allowed for quite a lot of refactoring. Where removal wasn't outright required, all instances of AlbumGroup have been replaced with AlbumType
- User no longer exposes market, so getMarketOfCurrentUser now simply tries to guess the market through the PC's locale. This means that, should the locale not match the current Spotify user, new releases get published at incorrect times. Maybe I can improve this at some point
- Release crawls of followed artists will now only issue two requests for albums/singles with a maximum of 10 results each. Compilations are completely ignored (they never get released anyway).
- Get artists doesn't allow for bulk fetch anymore, only individual ones. This will slow down the crawl process a lot, but there's nothing I can do.
- All instances of PlaylistTrack::getTrack have been changed to PlaylistTrack::getItem
- Playlist creation endpoint has been simplified
- Max fetch limits have been reduced new lowered values (10 instead of 50)
- Also finally updated Java, Spring, and Gradle while I was at it

commits.author: sebpet182
commits.message:
Fixed the login process, which broke after Spotify enforced a new standard for how the Redirect URIs must be set up (https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/web-api/concepts/redirect_uri):
- Replaced all instances of localhost with 127.0.0.1
- Replaced all instances of /login-callback with /callback
- Updated Readme to accommodate the changes
